newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia's Taylor says he was ambushed by gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Liberia's Taylor says he was ambushed by gunmen.

text.p: Liberia's chief warlord Charles Taylor said he escaped an assassination attempt on Thursday when gunmen ambushed him inside the presidential palace in Monrovia.

Taylor's senior aide and two other people died in the commando-style attack by gunmen who forced their way into the Executive Mansion in jeeps. Panic gripped the capital still recovering from devastating ethnic warfare in April and May.
The incident illustrates the fragility of the latest peace process in Liberia which has been tested by outbreaks of fighting in parts of the country and recent tension in Monrovia.
The commander of the ECOMOG African peacekeeping force sent out tanks and deployed troops in the city. He also extended a night curfew, which now starts three hours earlier from 7 p.m.
"I want to assure the people of Liberia that no stone will be left unturned to get to the root of the matter," Nigerian General Victor Malu said in a broadcast on Liberian state radio.
But several hours after the incident there was no word on the identity or whereabouts of the gunmen.

Malu said there was an explosion followed by an exchange of small arms fire on the sixth floor of the Executive Mansion. The presidential office and residence complex now serves largely for meetings of Liberia's interim ruling council. "At present we

have three dead bodies including one of Charles Taylor's senior aides," Malu said. A Nigerian captain assigned to Taylor was hit in the back but survived. Radio reports said 10 people died in the attack.
Malu said the casualties were from an exchange of fire between Taylor's security and the attackers.
Taylor, who started Liberia's civil war in 1989 but is now on the ruling council, described the attack in a radio speech.

"As I entered the sixth floor of the Executive Mansion I came under a hail of fire in which my senior aide-de-camp Jackson Manley and my ECOMOG (military) aide-de-camp and several of my senior staff were wounded," he said on his Kiss FM radio.
"I was not hit, through the mercy of God," he added.

Taylor did not say who could have carried out the attack. But Kiss FM quoted him as accusing forces of rival ethnic Krahn warlords George Boley and General Roosevelt Johnson as well as civilian council member Oscar Quiah. It did not elaborate.
Both Boley and Quiah went on radio to demand a thorough probe into the incident. Boley also denied involvement.
The Boley and Johnson were allied against a rival militia coalition dominated by Taylor in fighting in April and May.
The warfare ruined the capital Monrovia and derailed a delicate 1995 regional accord on ending the civil war.
The United States evacuated foreigners and sent Marines to protect its embassy. Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 and has traditional links with the United States.

A witness who was near the Executive Mansion said the unidentified attackers overran a checkpoint at the entrance to the mansion, which is guarded by troops of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG West African peacekeeping force stationed in Liberia.

"There was an attack on the mansion and shooting broke out," one witness said. "Shops, businesses, markets and schools closed hurriedly and traffic came to a halt. People started running... some with their belongings."
The attack happened three days after ECOMOG began to deploy across the country in earnest to start disarming guerrillas under a new peace deal.

Taylor said he did not expect the attack to affect the latest peace signed last August setting a new disarmemnt timetable and elections for next May. Taylor has already declared he will run for president.
